npmatch: a tiered workflow for organization record linkage

Source: R/npmatch-package.R
npmatch-package.Rd

npmatch manages the steps of matching organization records to a reference database when no shared identifier exists. The steps are generic; the nonprofit case the package ships wired for — federal registrants (SAM) to the IRS Business Master File — is one deployment of the framework, not a requirement of it.

Details

Six tiers, each a separable concern:

  1. Alias enumeration — every name and address an entity is known by. Supplied by matchdb: pass the object its md_compile() or md_reference() returns straight to np_cascade() as reference.

  2. Input standardization — np_query() / np_reference() map any dataset onto the canonical fields, then np_normalize() (from npnormalize, re-exported here) builds the name and address keys.

  3. Data pre-prep — the corpus statistics that make a token or an address informative: np_ref_index(), np_token_idf(), np_name_freq(), np_addr_freq(). Computed once over the whole reference, or taken precomputed from a matchdb reference.

  4. Candidate generation — np_block() / np_block_union() keep the pair set tractable; np_compare() scores each field, over reclin2.

  5. Tiered adjudication — np_score() combines the fields, np_veto() applies hard and soft do-not-match rules, np_select() picks the best candidate per query, np_tier() sorts into YES / MAYBE / NO.

  6. Packaging for review — np_route() emits the accepted crosswalk, the candidate-level review queue and the unmatched set; np_label_frame() emits training data and np_as_prompt() LLM prompts.

np_cascade() runs tiers 2–5 as progressive blocking passes (the scalable path) and np_match() in a single pass; np_route() then does tier 6 on the result. np_run_batches() chunks a large source over np_cascade() and routes each chunk, and the stage drivers (np_stage1_run() and its siblings) wrap the whole thing in an on-disk run project.
